To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

micro features are more effective than aggregated features for AES and that micro features and a mixture of micro features and aggregate features provide a greater range of features for providing formative feedback to users.

the use of micro features in AES systems outperforms the use of aggregated feature alone and that the combination of micro features with aggregated features in AES systems is superior to AES models based on the use of micro and aggregated features alone.
micro features and aggregated micro features outperform aggregated features alone in the context of AES.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to provide the most useful feedback to students writing in a foreign language.
the development and testing of automatic scoring and feedback systems for essays and other forms of writing.
the question of how to aggregate the features that are used to predict essay quality in order to provide feedback on the essays.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of micro features and the combination of micro features, and aggregated features are the best methods to use in the development of AES and feedback systems.
micro feature based AES models outperform aggregated feature based AES models in both accuracy of scores and in the variety of linguistic features that can be used to provide feedback.
the results indicate that AES models based upon micro features or a combination of micro and aggregated features are more effective than those based solely on aggregated features.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more information you have, the more accurate your model can be.
we have developed an AES model that is more accurate and more informative than the current state-of-the-art.
we have shown that it is not necessary to use aggregated features in AES systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of aggregated linguistic features alone in AES systems is not as beneficial as using a combination of aggregated features and micro features.
the use of micro features in AES models is more beneficial than the use of aggregated measures of linguistic complexity.
micro features are more effective in predicting essay quality than the use of aggregated micro features or the combination of micro and aggregated features.
